references.text: Moses appoints Joshua as leader by the Lord's command, which corresponds to Moses giving Joshua his charge.
Describes the victory over King Og of Bashan, one of the two kings mentioned in the verse.
Describes the victory over Sihon, king of the Amorites, the other of the two kings mentioned.
The Lord assures that He will do to the enemies as He did with Sihon and Og.
Moses encourages Joshua and assures him that the Lord will go before him and drive out the nations, just as He did with the two kings.
The Lord speaks to Joshua after Moses' death and confirms the promise to give them the lands they are to conquer.
Rahab confirms that the people of Canaan had heard about what the Lord did to the two Amorite kings, Sihon and Og.
Moses reminds the people that the Lord their God will fight for them, just as He did in Egypt.
Moses encourages Israel not to fear the nations but to remember what the Lord did to Egypt and will do to all peoples.
